goals: mechanistic: quantify how elevation (via lapse rate) controls snowmelt-onset DOY across the Naches SNOTEL sites
sub-goal: resolve the local temperature/precip lapse rate between stations on the same ridge
validation: reproduce observed SWE and melt-onset DOY at each SNOTEL station

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column carries the snowpack energy balance and SWE needed for melt-onset timing; SNOTEL gives co-located SWE for validation. The stations dictate placement.

answerable: validation of ELM SWE and melt-onset DOY against co-located SNOTEL SWE at each station (given station-appropriate forcing)
characterizing melt-onset in a fixed climate at each station location

not_answerable.aspect: elevation control on snowmelt-onset DOY as an elevation/climate signal
not_answerable.why: framework applies uniform forcing to single columns; under uniform atmosphere the melt-timing spread between columns reflects soil/column differences, not the elevation-driven lapse-rate signal the question targets
not_answerable.needs: elevation-downscaled forcing (lapse-rate-adjusted T, precip phase/amount, radiation, humidity per column)

not_answerable.aspect: resolving the local lapse rate between stations on the same ridge
not_answerable.why: the lapse rate is an input to the forcing, not an emergent model output; the stack has no mechanism to derive or apply a between-station lapse rate
not_answerable.needs: elevation-downscaled forcing with a configurable/derivable lapse rate; a forcing dataset or downscaling method that resolves ridge-scale gradients

sampling_strategy.approach: station-pinned validation with conditional light exploratory infill on the best-separated ridge pair
sampling_strategy.n_justification: The primary 'columns' are the 6 SNOTEL stations themselves (validation-pinned, count set by data). Exploratory columns are added ONLY to interpolate the ridge lapse rate between a well-separated station pair (2-3 intermediate-elevation points on that ridge); this is only meaningful once elevation-downscaled forcing exists, so it is flagged conditional. No dense grid is justified for a per-station question.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns exactly at the 6 SNOTEL locations (downstream expander pins them to station coordinates/elevations); place the ~3 exploratory columns along the ridge connecting the two stations with the largest elevation separation, to resolve the between-station lapse rate.
sampling_strategy.replication: None — each station is unique; replication adds no information under a fixed forcing per location.

sampling_plan.reason: One ELM column pinned to each SNOTEL station to compare modeled SWE / melt-onset DOY directly against co-located observations across the elevation range.
Intermediate-elevation columns along the best-separated same-ridge station pair to interpolate the local lapse rate — only interpretable once elevation-downscaled forcing is implemented.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — derive melt-onset DOY from modeled and observed SWE time series at each station and compare per station
validation_design.metric: bias in DOY (days), mean absolute error across stations

validation_design.comparison: co-located — full-season SWE curve at each station

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: native soil at each station; forcing 1980-2018 — CONDITIONAL on elevation-downscaled forcing (see requires_capabilities)

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-downscaled forcing (lapse-rate-adjusted T, precip phase/amount, radiation, humidity per column)
requires_capabilities.why: elevation controls melt-onset via the atmospheric lapse rate; uniform forcing cannot produce an elevation/climate signal
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire primary mechanism (elevation -> melt-onset DOY) and any physically meaningful per-station melt-timing validation

requires_capabilities.capability: configurable/derivable local lapse rate resolving ridge-scale gradients
requires_capabilities.why: the user explicitly wants the between-station lapse rate on the same ridge, which is a forcing property, not an ELM output
requires_capabilities.blocks: the 'resolve the local lapse rate' sub-goal and the exploratory ridge-infill columns

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL SWE ingest + melt-onset DOY extraction
requires_capabilities.why: validation requires reading station SWE time series and deriving a consistent melt-onset metric from both model and obs
requires_capabilities.blocks: validation of SWE and melt-onset DOY

requires_capabilities.capability: snow/SWE output at daily resolution + model spin-up
requires_capabilities.why: melt-onset DOY needs sub-monthly SWE output and an equilibrated snowpack/soil state
to pin columns to SNOTEL locations and assign each its elevation for the downscaling
requires_capabilities.blocks: column placement and per-column forcing adjustment

assumptions: The 6 SNOTEL stations lie within the Naches HUC bbox and their coordinates/elevations are resolvable downstream.
At least two stations share a ridge with sufficient elevation separation to define a local lapse rate (needed for the sub-goal).
1980-2018 forcing overlaps the SNOTEL records enough to compare climatological melt-onset.
Soil differences between stations are secondary to the elevation/climate control on melt timing.
open_questions: Should the lapse rate be prescribed (e.g. a fixed environmental value) or empirically derived from station observations, and if derived, from what data?
Which forcing product will supply the elevation downscaling (e.g. a gridded reanalysis with a downscaling scheme), and at what horizontal resolution?
Are the 6 SNOTEL stations distributed across enough distinct ridges/aspects that aspect (not just elevation) needs to be a driver?
Do you want per-year melt-onset (interannual variability) or a climatological mean melt-onset DOY per station?
